title: Psalms Chapter 38 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 38 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 38 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 38.

questions.question: In Psalms 38:1, what does David ask the LORD not to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Rebuke him in wrath
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:1 states, 'O LORD, rebuke me not in thy wrath: neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 38:2, what sticks fast in David?
questions.correctAnswer: Thine arrows
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:2 says, 'For thine arrows stick fast in me, and thy hand presseth me sore.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 38:3 says there is no soundness in David's bones because of his sin.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:3 states, '...neither is there any rest in my bones because of my sin.'

questions.question: What does David describe his iniquities as in Psalms 38:4?
questions.correctAnswer: As a heavy burden
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:4 says, 'For mine iniquities are gone over mine head: as an heavy burden they are too heavy for me.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 38:5, why do David's wounds stink and are corrupt?
questions.correctAnswer: Because of his foolishness
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:5 states, 'My wounds stink and are corrupt because of my foolishness.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 38:6 says David goes rejoicing all day long.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:6 says, 'I am troubled; I am bowed down greatly; I go mourning all the day long.'

questions.question: What loathsome condition is mentioned in Psalms 38:7?
options: Loins filled with a loathsome disease
questions.correctAnswer: Loins filled with a loathsome disease
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:7 states, 'For my loins are filled with a loathsome disease: and there is no soundness in my flesh.'

questions.question: What is David's condition in Psalms 38:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Feeble and sore broken
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:8 says, 'I am feeble and sore broken: I have roared by reason of the disquietness of my heart.'

questions.question: What does David say is before the LORD in Psalms 38:9?
questions.correctAnswer: All his desire
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:9 states, 'Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 38:10 says David's heart panteth and his strength faileth him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:10 says, 'My heart panteth, my strength faileth me: as for the light of mine eyes, it also is gone from me.'

questions.question: Who stands aloof from David's sore according to Psalms 38:11?
questions.correctAnswer: My lovers and my friends
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:11 states, 'My lovers and my friends stand aloof from my sore; and my kinsmen stand afar off.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 38:12, what do those who seek David's life do?
questions.correctAnswer: Lay snares for him
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:12 says, 'They also that seek after my life lay snares for me.'

questions.question: In Psalms 38, which comes first?
options: David asks the LORD not to rebuke him in wrath
David states his friends stand aloof
David says his loins are filled with a loathsome disease
questions.correctAnswer: David asks the LORD not to rebuke him in wrath
questions.explanation: The first verse, Psalms 38:1, contains David asking the LORD not to rebuke him in wrath, which precedes the other listed events.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 38:13, David was as a deaf man who heard not and as a dumb man who opened not his mouth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:13 states, 'But I, as a deaf man, heard not; and I was as a dumb man that openeth not his mouth.'

questions.question: What is David's hope according to Psalms 38:15?
questions.correctAnswer: In the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:15 says, 'For in thee, O LORD, do I hope: thou wilt hear, O Lord my God.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 38 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 38 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 38:9, what does the psalmist say about his desires and groaning?
options: His desires are hidden from the Lord, but his groaning is known to Him
All his desires are before the Lord, and his groaning is not hidden from Him
His desires are sinful and his groaning is ignored by the Lord
He hides his desires and groanings from everyone
questions.correctAnswer: All his desires are before the Lord, and his groaning is not hidden from Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:9 clearly states that the psalmist's desires and groanings are fully before God, showing his openness and trust. This aligns with verses 15 and 21 where he hopes and calls upon the Lord for help.

questions.question: What physical condition does the psalmist describe in Psalms 38:10?
options: His heart is joyful and his strength is renewed
His heart panteth, his strength faileth, and the light of his eyes is gone
He is full of energy and his eyes shine brightly
He feels physically well but spiritually weak
questions.correctAnswer: His heart panteth, his strength faileth, and the light of his eyes is gone
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:10 describes deep physical and emotional exhaustion, indicating the psalmist's profound distress, which connects to his mourning in verses 6 and 8.

questions.question: How do the psalmist's friends and kinsmen respond to his suffering according to Psalms 38:11?
options: They come close to comfort and support him
They stand aloof and keep afar off
They send gifts and encourage him
They ignore him because they do not know
questions.correctAnswer: They stand aloof and keep afar off
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:11 states that even his closest relations avoid him in his affliction, illustrating his isolation. This contrasts with his calling on the Lord in verses 15 and 21 for help.

questions.question: What do the enemies of the psalmist do as described in Psalms 38:12?
options: They pray for his healing and peace
They seek to help him in his troubles
They lay snares and speak mischievous things, imagining deceits all day
questions.correctAnswer: They lay snares and speak mischievous things, imagining deceits all day
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 38:12, the psalmist faces active hostility from those who seek to harm him, which adds to his distress mentioned in verses 10 and 11.

questions.question: How does the psalmist respond to the malicious actions of his enemies in Psalms 38:13?
options: He loudly rebukes them and defends himself
He ignores them as a deaf man and remains silent like a dumb man
questions.correctAnswer: He ignores them as a deaf man and remains silent like a dumb man
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:13 shows the psalmist's humility and restraint, choosing not to respond to evil with words, which relates to the silence described in verse 14.

questions.question: What is the significance of the psalmist being 'as a man that heareth not, and in whose mouth are no reproofs' in Psalms 38:14?
options: He refuses to listen to advice and speaks harshly
He is unable to hear and does not speak to others
He remains silent and does not offer reproof, showing patient submission
questions.correctAnswer: He remains silent and does not offer reproof, showing patient submission
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:14 illustrates the psalmist’s patient humility in suffering, choosing silence over confrontation, supporting the attitude described in verse 13 and his hope in God in verse 15.

questions.question: What reason does the psalmist give for his hope in the LORD in Psalms 38:15?
options: Because the LORD will ignore his prayers
Because the LORD is distant and weak
Because the LORD will hear him
Because the LORD has forgotten him
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD will hear him
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:15 states the psalmist’s confident hope that God will hear his prayers, which provides comfort amidst his suffering described in previous verses such as 9 and 10.

questions.question: What does the psalmist fear will happen if God does not hear him according to Psalms 38:16?
options: His enemies will rejoice and magnify themselves over him
His friends will come to his aid
He will find peace and rest
questions.correctAnswer: His enemies will rejoice and magnify themselves over him
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:16 highlights the psalmist’s fear that without God’s intervention, his enemies will triumph, connecting with the hostile actions described in verse 12 and his hope in verse 15.

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe his sorrow and readiness to halt in Psalms 38:17?
options: He is ready to halt and sorrow is continually before him
He has no sorrow and walks confidently
He is indifferent to his condition
questions.correctAnswer: He is ready to halt and sorrow is continually before him
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:17 expresses the psalmist’s deep ongoing sorrow and physical weakness, reinforcing the themes of distress and dependence on God seen in verses 10 and 15.

questions.question: What spiritual practice does the psalmist commit to in Psalms 38:18?
options: He declares his iniquity and is sorry for his sin
He hides his sins and refuses to repent
He blames others for his troubles
questions.correctAnswer: He declares his iniquity and is sorry for his sin
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:18 highlights confession and repentance as key elements of the psalmist’s response to sin, complementing his plea for God’s help in verses 21 and 22.

questions.question: According to Psalms 38:19, how does the psalmist describe his enemies?
options: They are weak and few in number
They are lively, strong, and wrongfully multiplied
questions.correctAnswer: They are lively, strong, and wrongfully multiplied
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:19 portrays the enemies as numerous and vigorous, intensifying the psalmist’s need for God’s protection mentioned in verses 21 and 22.

questions.question: What does Psalms 38:20 say about those who render evil for good?
options: They are the psalmist's adversaries because he follows good
They are friends who misunderstand him
questions.correctAnswer: They are the psalmist's adversaries because he follows good
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:20 explains that the psalmist faces opposition from those who repay kindness with evil, emphasizing the challenge of maintaining integrity described in verses 18 and 19.

questions.question: What plea does the psalmist make to the LORD in Psalms 38:21?
options: Forsake me not, O LORD; be not far from me
Let my enemies triumph over me
questions.correctAnswer: Forsake me not, O LORD; be not far from me
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:21 is a heartfelt plea for God's nearness and support, reinforcing the themes of trust and dependence that run throughout the chapter, especially in verses 15 and 22.

questions.question: How does Psalms 38:22 summarize the psalmist’s request to God?
options: Make haste to help me, O Lord my salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Make haste to help me, O Lord my salvation
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:22 concludes the psalmist’s urgent appeal for God's immediate help, tying together the distress and hope expressed from verses 9 through 21.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 38:12, the psalmist’s enemies only speak truth and kindness about him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:12 states that the enemies speak mischievous things and imagine deceits all day, which is the opposite of truth and kindness.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 38 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 38.

questions.question: According to Psalms 38:17, what is continually before the psalmist?
questions.correctAnswer: His sorrow
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:17 states, 'For I am ready to halt, and my sorrow is continually before me,' indicating that sorrow is always present before the psalmist.

questions.question: In Psalms 38:18, what does the psalmist declare he will do regarding his sin?
questions.correctAnswer: Be sorry for it
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'For I will declare mine iniquity; I will be sorry for my sin,' showing the psalmist's repentance.

questions.question: Psalms 38:19 describes the psalmist’s enemies as:
questions.correctAnswer: Lively and strong
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'But mine enemies are lively, and they are strong,' emphasizing the threat they pose.

questions.question: What reason does the psalmist give in Psalms 38:20 for why some render evil for good against him?
options: Because he follows the thing that good is
questions.correctAnswer: Because he follows the thing that good is
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'They also that render evil for good are mine adversaries; because I follow the thing that good is.'

questions.question: What plea does the psalmist make to the LORD in Psalms 38:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Forsake me not, O LORD
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks, 'Forsake me not, O LORD: O my God, be not far from me,' pleading for God's presence and help.

questions.question: In Psalms 38:22, how does the psalmist ask the Lord to respond?
questions.correctAnswer: Make haste to help me
questions.explanation: The psalmist urgently requests, 'Make haste to help me, O Lord my salvation,' showing his desperate need.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of sorrow and repentance found in Psalms 38:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 51:17
questions.explanation: Psalm 51:17 emphasizes a broken and contrite heart, paralleling the repentance and sorrow in Psalms 38:18.

questions.question: The Hebrew word for 'iniquity' as used in Psalms 38:18 primarily means:
questions.correctAnswer: Unrighteousness or guilt
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'awon' used here signifies moral guilt or wrongdoing, aligning with the psalmist’s confession in Psalms 38:18.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 38:17–22 to emphasize the psalmist's plea for help?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The structure of verses 17–22 forms a chiasm, focusing on the central plea for God's presence and help (Psalms 38:21–22).

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 38:19, the psalmist says his enemies are weak and few in number.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:19 states the enemies are 'lively, and they are strong,' contradicting the statement.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 38:21 contains a plea for God not to be far from the psalmist.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks, 'O my God, be not far from me,' expressing a desire for God's nearness (Psalms 38:21).

questions.question: How does Psalms 38:16 describe the psalmist’s fear concerning his enemies' reaction when he stumbles?
options: They will rejoice and magnify themselves against him
questions.correctAnswer: They will rejoice and magnify themselves against him
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:16 says, 'when my foot slippeth, they magnify themselves against me,' showing the psalmist’s concern about his enemies' rejoicing.

questions.question: What physical condition does the psalmist describe in Psalms 38:10 as a result of his suffering?
options: My heart panteth and my strength faileth me
My eyes are full of tears
questions.correctAnswer: My heart panteth and my strength faileth me
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:10 states, 'My heart panteth, my strength faileth me,' describing physical weakness due to distress.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of unjust suffering and enemies seeking to harm found in Psalms 38:19-20?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Peter 3:14
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 3:14 speaks about suffering for righteousness and being harassed by evildoers, paralleling Psalms 38:19-20.

questions.question: In the ancient Near Eastern context, what does the psalmist's description of 'arrows' and 'hand pressing sore' in Psalms 38:2 symbolize?
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment and affliction
questions.explanation: Arrows and pressing hand metaphorically describe God's chastening and spiritual affliction as understood in ancient Near Eastern imagery (Psalms 38:2).

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 38 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 38 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What aspect of God's nature is primarily revealed in Psalms 38:1 when David pleads, "O LORD, rebuke me not in thy wrath"?
options: God's wrath directed only at the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: God's merciful restraint in judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 38:1 shows David asking God not to rebuke him in His wrath or chasten him in hot displeasure, implying God's merciful control over His righteous judgment rather than immediate punishment. This reveals God's attribute of mercy (Exodus 34:6).

questions.question: In Psalms 38:4, David says his iniquities "are gone over mine head: as an heavy burden they are too heavy for me." What doctrine does this verse illustrate?
options: The weight and guilt of sin
questions.correctAnswer: The weight and guilt of sin
questions.explanation: This verse teaches the doctrine of the burden and guilt sin places on the sinner, showing that sin is heavy and overwhelming. It reflects the biblical teaching on the seriousness of sin (Romans 3:23).

questions.question: How does Psalms 38:9 reveal the believer's relationship with God in times of distress?
options: Believers hide their desires from God
God is unaware of human groaning
All desires and groaning are known by God
Believers must remain silent before God
questions.correctAnswer: All desires and groaning are known by God
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states that all David's desires and groaning are before God and not hidden, revealing God's omniscience and intimate knowledge of the believer's inner struggles (Psalm 34:15).

questions.question: What divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 38:15 where David says, "For in thee, O LORD, do I hope: thou wilt hear, O Lord my God"?
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness to hear prayer
questions.explanation: This verse emphasizes God's faithful attentiveness to the prayers of His people, revealing that God hears and responds to the hope placed in Him (1 John 5:14).

questions.question: Considering Psalms 38:7 and Psalms 38:3 together, what theological truth is taught about sin's effect on the human person?
options: Sin only affects the soul, not the body
Sin causes spiritual and physical distress
Sin is easily ignored without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Sin causes spiritual and physical distress
questions.explanation: Both verses highlight that sin results in deep bodily and spiritual suffering: no soundness in flesh and loathsome disease (Psalms 38:3,7), illustrating the comprehensive impact of sin (Isaiah 1:5-6).

questions.question: What do Psalms 38:11 and Psalms 38:12 together teach about the social consequences of sin and suffering?
options: Believers will always be supported by friends
Sin leads to alienation and enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to alienation and enemies
questions.explanation: These verses show that David’s suffering results in friends standing aloof and enemies plotting harm, teaching that sin and distress often bring social rejection and hostility (John 15:18-20).

questions.question: How does David's response in Psalms 38:13-14, being "as a deaf man" and "as a dumb man that openeth not his mouth," teach about sanctification under persecution?
options: Believers should respond aggressively to enemies
Silence and trust in God are appropriate under attack
Ignoring God is the best response to hardship
Rebuking enemies is a duty of the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Silence and trust in God are appropriate under attack
questions.explanation: David’s silence amidst slander and deceit shows a sanctified response of trust and restraint, not retaliating but trusting God’s justice (1 Peter 2:23).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight emerges from Psalms 38:18 and Psalms 38:21 about repentance and divine help?
options: Repentance is unnecessary if God helps
Confession of sin precedes earnest plea for God's nearness
questions.correctAnswer: Confession of sin precedes earnest plea for God's nearness
questions.explanation: Verse 18 emphasizes declaring and sorrowing for sin, while verse 21 shows the plea for God not to forsake, teaching repentance as a prerequisite for seeking God's sustaining presence (1 John 1:9).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 38 portrays God as harsh and unloving due to the intense suffering described. What does Psalms 38:22 actually teach about God's character?
options: God is indifferent to human suffering
God is slow to help and often absent
God swiftly aids those who call upon Him
questions.correctAnswer: God swiftly aids those who call upon Him
questions.explanation: Verse 22 is a plea for God to "Make haste to help me," showing that God is portrayed as a Savior who responds promptly to cries for help, affirming His loving and compassionate nature (Psalm 34:17).

questions.question: What do Psalms 38:5 and Psalms 38:6 collectively reveal about the consequences of foolishness and sin on the believer's condition?
options: Sin causes corruption and prolonged mourning
questions.correctAnswer: Sin causes corruption and prolonged mourning
questions.explanation: Verse 5 describes wounds that stink and corrupt due to foolishness, and verse 6 describes mourning all day, showing sin and folly produce spiritual and emotional decay and sorrow (Romans 7:24).

questions.question: Which doctrine is demonstrated by David's admission in Psalms 38:17, "For I am ready to halt, and my sorrow is continually before me"?
options: The ongoing effect of conviction and brokenness
questions.correctAnswer: The ongoing effect of conviction and brokenness
questions.explanation: David’s continual sorrow and inability to stand firmly illustrates the doctrine that true repentance involves ongoing brokenness and conviction over sin (Psalm 51:17).

questions.question: How does Psalms 38:19-20 together describe the nature of opposition faced by the godly, and what theological principle does this illustrate?
options: Opposition is only from external physical enemies
The godly face opposition even when pursuing good
Enemies are always justified in their hatred
questions.correctAnswer: The godly face opposition even when pursuing good
questions.explanation: These verses teach that enemies wrongfully oppose the righteous who follow good, emphasizing that faithful obedience can provoke hostility (John 15:18-20).

questions.question: What theological truth about prayer and hope is expressed by combining Psalms 38:10 and Psalms 38:15?
options: Loss of strength means loss of hope
Physical weakness can coexist with confident hope in God
Prayer is only effective when one is strong
questions.correctAnswer: Physical weakness can coexist with confident hope in God
questions.explanation: Verse 10 describes physical weakness and loss of sight, while verse 15 expresses confident hope that God will hear, teaching that hope and prayer persist despite physical frailty (2 Corinthians 12:9).

questions.question: What attribute of God is best illustrated in Psalms 38:2 where David says, "For thine arrows stick fast in me, and thy hand presseth me sore"?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s righteous judgment and discipline
questions.explanation: The imagery of arrows and pressing hand symbolizes God’s active righteous judgment and chastening of sin, reflecting His holiness and justice (Hebrews 12:6).

questions.question: How does Psalms 38:16 relate to the broader biblical narrative of the believer’s struggle with enemies and temptation?
options: Believers never face opposition when they stumble
Enemies rejoice over the believer’s failures
Temptation is always external and physical
questions.correctAnswer: Enemies rejoice over the believer’s failures
questions.explanation: Verse 16 warns that if the believer’s foot slips, enemies magnify themselves, showing the reality of spiritual warfare and temptation where foes exploit failures (Ephesians 6:12).
